newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY MAIN FARMERS UNION MULL NATIONWIDE PROTEST.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY MAIN FARMERS UNION MULL NATIONWIDE PROTEST.

text.p: Hungary's biggest farmers union was preparing on Friday an appeal for talks with Prime Minister Gyula Horn to overhaul Hungary's agriculture, backed with a threat of demonstrations if talks are refused.

MOSZ delegates, representing over 1,100 cooperatives and farming companies, said during a heated debate at its headquarters the government had bowed to pressure from a local group of protestors last week but had been disregarding MOSZ complaints for years.
"We will contact Horn and other relevant government officials today and ask for talks on our list of demands," one union leader told delegates.

Last week, the government agreed to demands from a group of protesting farmers from central Hungary's Kiskoros to reduce social security contributions but stopped short of reversing 1997 farm taxation and social security rules

The farmers, who had set up roadblocks and have since formed their own organisation, METESZ, hardened their stance and snubbed Horn's invitation for further talks after unsucessful negotiations with finance and agriculture ministry officials.
Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy's said on Wednesday he was unwilling to agree to "any substantial change affecting the proportionate sharing of tax burdens".

With Friday's MOSZ meeting still underway, Agriculture Minister Frigyes Nagy, who was presenting the government's farming policy draft to journalists, said the cabinet was not open for talks about further concessions to farmers.
"Even if there is a demonstration, the government will not negotiate," Nagy said.
METESZ has again set up roadblocks around the central Hungarian town of Kiskoros.
